Unescaped embed URL goes into a raw-HTML post, so an anonymous visitor can store XSS `url` is interpolated into `#{url}` with no escaping, and the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns `raw` as is (app/models/post.rb:133). The URL can come from an anonymous request: `EmbedController#best` passes `params[:embed_url]` to the RetrieveTopic job (embed_controller.rb:15), and `TopicRetriever` only checks that `URI(@embed_url).host` matches embeddable_host (topic_retriever.rb:15). `'` is a legal URI character, so a value like `http:///?'onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)` passes that check. If the page answers 200, `import_remote` → `import` stores an attribute-injected ``, which Nokogiri re-serializes as a real event handler (line 61-75). That HTML is then served from the forum's origin, both in the topic and in `embed/best` (`raw post.cooked`). Fix: escape the URL (`ERB::Util.html_escape`), and run raw_html content through a sanitizer before storing it.

raw_html posts skip all sanitizing, and edits keep the flag

With `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` verbatim. Feed items (poll_feed.rb:35, only `CGI.unescapeHTML`) and fetched pages are stored with no sanitizing, so any `<script>`, `<iframe>` or `on*` attribute in the feed or the embeddable site runs on the forum origin. The flag also stays set when the post is later edited through PostRevisor, so whoever can edit that post (its owner, or staff) can publish arbitrary HTML. Whitelist-sanitize the HTML when it is imported, or in this branch of `cook`.

The throttle is keyed per exact URL, so anonymous visitors can create topics without limit

The throttle is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, and `embed/best` takes requests from anyone whose Referer matches the host (embed_controller.rb:26; the Referer is client-controlled). Changing the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) gives a new key each time. Each new key costs one remote fetch, plus a full feed poll when polling is enabled (line 41). If the page answers, a new topic is created as embed_by_username, because TopicEmbed is unique on the raw embed_url string. Normalize the URL (strip the query and fragment) before checking and storing it, and add a global or per-IP rate limit.

The loading page reloads forever when retrieval can never succeed

Nothing bounds this wait. The page reloads every 30 s, and each reload hits `best` again, which enqueues another RetrieveTopic job (embed_controller.rb:15). Retrieval can fail for good in several ways: the host check fails (topic_retriever.rb:15), embed_by_username is not set (line 49-50), `open(url)` raises in `import_remote`, or `PostCreator` returns nil. In any of these cases the reader sees "Loading Discussion..." indefinitely, and one more job is queued every 30 s per open page. Cap the number of reloads, or show a failure state.

Disqus import no longer keeps the category or the original created_at

The `--category` option and the `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` it passed before were removed. Imported threads now land uncategorized and are dated at import time, with no warning. `import_remote` also fetches each `t[:link]` over the network, and any failure (404, timeout) raises and aborts the whole import partway through. Pass the category and created_at through `import` / `PostCreator` options, and rescue per-thread fetch errors.

`<%- end if %>` turns the next template statement into the `if` condition

ERB compiles this to `end if` followed by the next generated statement, which here is the buffer append for the logo link on line 8. Ruby parses that as `(if/else block) if (append logo link)`. So the condition runs first, and the logo gets emitted before the header button, reversing the intended order. Use `<%- end %>`.

Origin check is a substring match

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a prefix or substring of discourseUrl. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes for `https://forum.example.com/`. Today it can only resize the iframe, but compare the parsed origin exactly.

"is 404 without an embed_url" fails for a different reason than its name says

`ensure_embeddable` runs before `params.require`, and embeddable_host is not set in this example, so the request is rejected for the missing host, not for the missing embed_url. Set a host and a valid referer so the example actually exercises `params.require`.

`force: true` added to an already-shipped migration

Editing an existing migration has no effect on databases that already ran it. On any database where `top_topics` exists but the migration is re-run, it silently drops the table. Same pattern in create_topic_embeds. Drop `force: true` unless there is a specific reason for it.

Second `downsize` definition replaces the 5-argument one and breaks emoji resizing

Ruby keeps only the last definition of a method name. So `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 silently replaces `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145, and the method now takes 3 or 4 arguments. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14). Every run of that job will now raise ArgumentError, so custom emoji are never downsized. Give the new method its own name (for example `downsize_to(from, to, dimensions, opts)`), or have the controller pass a geometry string through a separate method. Then remove the dead definition at lines 145-147.

Hard-coded 10 MB client limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`

`validateUploadedFile` is called with `type` set to 'image' or 'attachment' (line 158). Before this change it used `max_<type>_size_kb`. Now both types are capped at a fixed 10 MB. Server-side downsizing only applies to images, yet attachments lose their configured limit too. If an admin set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB, the browser now rejects attachments the server would accept. If it is set below 10 MB, the alert no longer shows the real limit. Keep `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments and use the 10 MB pre-downsize cap only when `type === 'image'`. The 413 message at line 246 also shows a hard-coded 10 MB. That number is not tied to any setting or web-server config, so users may be told the wrong limit.

Does `tempfile.size` see the downsized file after ImageOptim rewrites it?

The loop rereads `tempfile.size` after each `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`. `convert_with` runs `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:160-165). If image_optim swaps in its result by renaming a new file over the path, the open Tempfile descriptor still points at the old, unlinked inode. In that case `tempfile.size` keeps returning the original size. The loop would then always run all 5 lossy passes, and `Upload.create_for` would get a stale size, or stale content if it reads from the descriptor. Have you checked that the size and content seen through `tempfile` change after a pass? Reading `File.size(tempfile.path)` would avoid depending on this.

No tests for the new automatic downsizing path

The pull request adds a downsizing loop in `create_upload` and changes the `OptimizedImage` resize/downsize API, but adds no specs. A spec that uploads an oversized image, and one covering `Jobs::ResizeEmoji`, would have caught the `downsize` arity break.

Crashes with a 500 when the user has no TopicUser row

`TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has never had a topic_users row for this topic. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and raises NoMethodError. A notification email does not need that row to exist; a mention in a topic the user never opened is one example. So the link in the email can fail with a server error. Fall back to `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row when it is missing and also publishes the MessageBus level change, or handle nil explicitly.

A GET request changes state, and each visit lowers the level one step The action changes the user's notification level on a plain GET (config/routes.rb:440-441). There is no CSRF token, because `check_xhr` is skipped (line 32). The change also steps down each time: watching/tracking goes to regular, and regular goes to muted. Three problems follow. (1) Any other site can embed `` and silently mute topics for a logged-in visitor. (2) Email link scanners and prefetchers fire the link without the user acting. (3) A user who opens the link twice, or reloads the page, ends up muted, not regular, and nothing tells them. Make the change idempotent: always set one target level (e.g. regular, or muted if already regular, but only through an explicit action). Better, show a confirmation page and apply the change through a POST/PUT.

Opening the unsubscribe route inside the app shows the message but changes nothing

Only the server action `topics#unsubscribe` changes the notification level. The Ember route's model hook only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which loads the topic view and never touches the unsubscribe endpoint. If the user reaches `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` inside the app (an in-app link, or Back/Forward after a cached load), the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the level is not changed. The user sees a wrong result with no warning. Either call the unsubscribe endpoint from the route (e.g. via `topic.details.updateNotifications`), or word the text so it does not claim a change happened.

The message says notifications stop even when the level only dropped to regular

When the starting level is watching or tracking, the server sets it to regular (topics_controller.rb:107-108). At regular the user still gets notifications for mentions, quotes and replies. "You will stop receiving notifications" overstates what happened. Consider showing the level that was actually set. The property name `stopNotificiationsText` is also misspelled; the template uses the same spelling.

New controller action and toggle logic are untested

The only spec change adds `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder spec. Nothing tests `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: the slug redirect, the watching→regular and regular→muted transitions, or the case with no TopicUser row.

Deleting the cache never invalidates connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing a stale cache status

`deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess`. The disconnect mutation next to it invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` (lines 61-64); this one invalidates nothing. In the event type Advanced tab (`packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-377`), `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` gets no `onChanged`, so nothing refetches. The query also uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. The result: after a successful delete, the dropdown still shows "Last updated: …" and the delete option, which tells the user the cache still exists. Fix: invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in this mutation's `onSettled`, as the disconnect mutation does.

Empty-data updateMany on every cache refresh, and the UI never reads its result

`updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs a write on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` (webhooks and cron), relying on Prisma to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` from an empty `data`. I'm not sure Prisma issues an UPDATE at all when `data` is empty. Either way, the cache status the UI shows comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-187`), and the `upsertCachedAvailability` upsert already sets that. Nothing in this PR reads the newly selected `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Consider dropping this call, or setting `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly if it is really needed.

Cache timestamp is always formatted as en-US

`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale and profile time zone, while the label around it is translated. Consider using the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) instead.

Cache status counts expired rows

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` takes `_max(updatedAt)` over every CalendarCache row of the credential, including rows past `expiresAt`. So the UI can report a cache that is no longer used. Also, the migration backfills `updatedAt` with NOW() for legacy rows, so right after deploy every existing cache shows as "updated" at migration time. Consider filtering on `expiresAt > now()`.

Delete-cache action now appears where connection modification is disabled

Before, no action was rendered when `disableConnectionModification` was true (the event type Advanced tab). Now the dropdown renders there whenever a Google cache exists, and it offers the destructive "Delete cached data" action. Is exposing cache deletion on the event type page intended?

Script only works on macOS and from one directory

`sed -i ''` is BSD syntax: GNU sed treats `''` as a file name and fails. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current directory, not the script's location, so running the script from the repository root writes to the directory above the repository. Consider resolving the path from `$(dirname "$0")` and using a portable in-place edit.

Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check, so double bookings become possible

When a slot falls on a date-override day and inside the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is true and the function returns `true` at line 134. It never reaches `busy.every(...)` at line 153. Existing bookings and calendar events on any day that has a date override stop blocking slots, so invitees can book over a meeting the host already has. Instead of returning `true` here, fall through to the busy check (skip only the working-hours check).

Working-hours check rejects a slot that falls outside any one range for that day, not outside all of them

`workingHours.find` returns true (slot rejected) as soon as one entry for the slot's weekday doesn't contain it. `getWorkingHours` (packages/lib/availability.ts:76-121) often emits several entries per weekday: one per availability range (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17), plus overflow entries when the organizer's local hours cross UTC midnight (lines 103-121). Any slot in one range lies outside the other, so every slot that day is removed. A UTC-8 organizer working 9-17 loses the 00:00-01:00 UTC part, and a split schedule loses every slot. The check should reject a slot only when no entry for that day contains it, i.e. `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`.

`end` is computed from the slot start, so slots running past the end of working hours are kept

`end` uses `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()`, the same value as `start`. `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore never catches a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them. Use `slotEndTime` here. A slot ending exactly at 00:00 also needs handling, since its minute value wraps to 0.

With multiple overrides on the same date, slots in all but one of them are rejected

`dateOverrides.find` returns true (slot rejected) when an override on the slot's date doesn't contain the slot. With two overrides on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), a 15:00 slot lies outside the first one, so it is dropped even though the second override allows it. The slot should be rejected only when it fits none of the matching overrides.

Override day is matched on the UTC calendar date (formatted in server-local time), not the organizer's date

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` gives the override start as a real UTC instant. It is then formatted with `dayjs()`'s default (server-local) zone and compared to `slotStartTime.format(...)` in UTC. For an organizer far from UTC, the override's UTC date can differ from the organizer's date. Example: a UTC+10 override for Nov 12, 08:00-12:00, starts Nov 11 22:00 UTC. Every Nov 11 UTC slot, including the organizer's normal Nov 11 working hours, then counts as 'on the override date but outside it' and is removed. Overridden slots after UTC midnight are also not matched. On a server not running in UTC, the two `format` calls also use different zones. Compare dates in the organizer's time zone (e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)` against the override's local date), or test the interval directly.

`===` between two Dayjs objects is always false

These are two distinct Dayjs instances, so the zero-length-override branch can never run. If it is meant to treat `start == end` as 'unavailable all day', use `.isSame(...)`. Otherwise, remove it.

An await in the catch block can throw and abort the whole cron batch

Before this change the catch only logged, so one failing reminder never stopped the loop. Now it calls `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` with no protection. If that update rejects, the error leaves the `for` loop and the handler, and every reminder after this one goes unscheduled for that run. It can reject because the row was deleted at the same time (booking cancelled or rescheduled → Prisma P2025), or because of a DB hiccup, which is often what made the attempt fail in the first place. The update in the `else` at line 179 sits inside the `try`, so it falls into this same catch and is a second chance to throw. Either wrap the increment in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany({ where: { id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`: it does not throw when the row is gone, and the atomic increment also avoids writing back a stale `reminder.retryCount + 1`.

SMS reminders are silently deleted after two failed attempts, about 30 minutes apart

The cron runs every 15 minutes (`.github/workflows/cron-scheduleSMSReminders.yml:8`). The count goes up on every thrown error (line 195) and every falsy `scheduleSMS` result (line 184). Once `retryCount > 1`, the next run's `deleteMany` removes the row. So two failures in a row delete the reminder for good, even when its send date is days away, with only a `console.log` left behind. Failures that clear on their own lead here too: a Twilio outage, the `checkSMSRateLimit` throw (twilioProvider.ts:97-102), or a team or user that is only briefly locked (`scheduleSMS` returns undefined at twilioProvider.ts:92-95). Before this change those reminders were retried on every run until `scheduledDate` passed. Now the attendee or organizer just never gets the reminder, and nothing shows it. Raise the threshold, or delete only when the reminder can no longer be scheduled (for example, `retryCount` over the limit and `scheduledDate` close). And log or record the drop where someone can see it.

The retryCount delete branch has no method filter

The second `OR` branch deletes every `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, whatever its method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS). Right now only this SMS cron writes `retryCount`, so nothing else is affected yet. But the column is on the shared model, so the moment the email or WhatsApp crons start counting retries, this SMS job will delete their rows. Put `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` on this branch as well.

Fragments are returned without outer parentheses, so a caller's added AND binds to only part of the OR

The org/team authorization fragments come out as `(A) OR (B)` (lines 171-174, 204-207). The eventType filter also comes out unwrapped: `("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)` (line 106). `getBaseConditions` returns the auth fragment as is (line 75), and `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` are public. The point of this refactor is that callers splice the fragment into raw SQL. A caller that writes `WHERE ${base} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}` gets `(A) OR (B) AND createdAt >= …`, which SQL reads as `A OR (B AND …)`. Every team booking then skips the caller's date/status filter, the numbers come out wrong, and nothing reports an error. No caller exists yet, but this is the contract the next PR will build on. Fix: wrap every fragment the class returns, e.g. ``Prisma.sql`(${...})` ``, in the reduce results and in line 106.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy (it falls back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`, never null). Because of that, the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run. Simplify to: `filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${auth}) AND (${filter})` : auth`.

Looser public options type hides a missing teamId until runtime

The constructor used to accept the discriminated union, so `{ scope: "team" }` without `teamId` failed to compile. With `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, that call compiles. The zod parse at line 62 then fails, `options` becomes null, and the service quietly returns `1=0` (no data) with no error. Keep the union type for the constructor, or log or throw when validation fails.

Caching tests removed while the caching code remains

The `Caching` describe block was deleted, but `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still cache their results (insightsBooking.ts:83-95). No test covers that behaviour now. The `getBaseConditions` test also covers only the user scope. No test runs an org- or team-scope fragment against the database, which is where the `ANY(${array})` binding and OR precedence matter.

Google credential key is overwritten with a safeParse result object

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29). Line 97 assigns that wrapper to `key` and line 100 saves it as the credential key. The old code saved `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the data itself. After the first token refresh, every Google Calendar credential holds `{success:true,data:{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws. This hits all Google Calendar users, not just setups with credential sharing on. Fix: use `.data` here, or have the helper return the data.

Computed keys built from `z.string().toString()` create a single literal key, not a wildcard

`z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to "[object Object]". So the schema is `{access_token, "[object Object]": unknown}`. A `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, which means that in sync mode `data` contains only `access_token` plus the placeholder `refresh_token`. The expiry fields (`expires_in`, `expiry_date`), which the comment says should be kept, are dropped. Callers then persist credentials with no expiry. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`, or a `catchall`.

Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" is injected even when sync is off

The default runs on every path, not only in sync mode. In Office 365 Calendar, `refreshTokenResponseSchema.refresh_token` is optional (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:56), and the parsed data is spread over the stored credentials (line 264). When Microsoft omits a new refresh token, the real stored refresh token is replaced by the string "refresh_token" and saved (line 265-270). The next refresh then fails and the calendar stops working, with no visible error. Before this change, the old refresh token was kept. Apply the placeholder only in the sync branch, or skip it entirely when there is no refresh_token.

Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers expect a different shape

In sync mode this returns a `fetch` `Response`. Google expects a gaxios response with `.data` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95: `res?.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws). Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data.error` (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96, zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217). HubSpot treats the result as a token object. So with credential sharing on, refresh is broken for these apps. Only the fetch-based adapters (Zoom, Office 365, Webex, Lark) work. Normalise the return value, for example by parsing the JSON once, and adapt each caller to it.

Credential id is sent as the user id to the sync endpoint

`refreshOAuthTokens` takes a userId and posts it as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). Here `credentialId` is passed instead (the argument from line 69). The external app is therefore asked for the tokens of whichever user has an id equal to this credential's id. That could return another user's tokens, which would be stored on this credential. Pass `credential.userId`. This method only receives the id and key, so the userId needs to be threaded through.

`prisma` is used but never imported

The file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `@calcom/prisma`. The new `prisma.credential.update` call only resolves if a global `prisma` happens to exist. That global is set only for dev hot-reload caching, so in production `getClient` would throw a ReferenceError, and every Salesforce operation would reject. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`.

Salesforce refreshes unconditionally, skips the sync path, and then ignores the new token

Every time `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed, it calls the Salesforce token endpoint, even when the stored token is still valid. It calls `fetch` directly instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sharing never applies to Salesforce. It also uses `statusText !== "OK"` (line 86), which fails on HTTP/2 responses where statusText is empty; `response.ok` would be the reliable check. Finally, the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106), the old token, not `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

Malformed body or undecryptable keys produce an unhandled 500

`schema.parse` (line 31) and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (line 57-59) throw on bad input, and nothing catches them. The parent app gets an opaque 500 instead of a 400. Use `safeParse`, and wrap the decrypt step in try/catch so it returns 400. The handler also accepts any HTTP method; it should reject everything except POST.

Webhook secret compared with `!==`

The secret check is a plain string comparison, which is not constant-time. Consider `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and handle the case where the header arrives as an array.

Outgoing sync request carries no authentication

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no secret. The parent app cannot tell that the request comes from Cal.com, yet it answers with live access tokens. Consider sending `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, or a signature, in a header.

One failed SendGrid cancel stops every other cancellation, on every run

The whole loop sits inside one try. If `client.request` throws for any reminder (bad or expired batch_id, rate limit, a batch that was already cancelled), the loop exits. `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` never runs, and because Prisma promises are lazy, none of the deletes queued so far run either. The failing row keeps `cancelled: true` and stays in the `lte now+1h` window until line 34 removes it once its send time has passed. Every 15-minute run hits it first and aborts again, so reminders for other cancelled bookings in that window are never cancelled and get sent. The only trace is a console.log. Put the try/catch around each reminder (cancel, then delete that row) so one bad batch only affects itself.

Reminders due before the next cron run are no longer cancelled

Non-immediate cancellation now only sets `cancelled: true`. The SendGrid cancel happens in the cron (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-64), which runs every 15 minutes (.github/workflows/cron-scheduleEmailReminders.yml:8). Take a booking cancelled at :05 whose reminder is scheduled with SendGrid for :10. The :00 run has already passed and the :15 run is too late, so the attendee gets a reminder for a booking that no longer exists. Before this change the batch was cancelled right away. This affects every non-immediate caller: handleCancelBooking.ts:488, bookings.tsx:490, and workflows.tsx:378 and :576. To fix it, cancel immediately when the reminder's `scheduledDate` falls before the next cron run, for example within the next hour, which matches the cron's own window. That means passing `scheduledDate` (or the reminder object) in.

Reminder cancellation is no longer awaited before the response

Before this change the reminder row deletes went into `prismaPromises` and were awaited. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are started inside `forEach` and never awaited, so the handler can respond before the `cancelled: true` update (or the Twilio cancel) finishes. On a serverless runtime that freezes after the response, that work can be lost, and the cron would then send the reminder for the cancelled booking. The same applies to bookings.tsx:489, which used to `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`. Collecting the promises and awaiting them with the other Prisma work fixes it.

try/catch cannot catch errors from these un-awaited async calls

Both delete functions are async and are called without `await` inside `forEach`, so their rejections never reach this `catch`. Both functions already catch their own errors anyway, which makes this `log.error` dead code. Either drop the try/catch or collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` them inside it.

Why immediate SendGrid cancel on reschedule but deferred everywhere else?

This PR defers email cancellation to the cron on booking cancel and on requestReschedule (bookings.tsx:490), presumably to stay under SendGrid's limit on concurrently cancelled or paused batches. A normal reschedule here (and workflow or step deletion, workflows.tsx:214 and :521) still cancels immediately with `immediateDelete: true`. If that limit is the reason for the change, many reschedules at once could still hit it, and the cancel would fail silently (it is only logged), so the old-time reminder goes out. isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: wrong offset and inverted condition

The encoded prefix is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2)` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117`), so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. On top of that, the code returns `false` when the shortcut *matches*, which is the reverse of what the matcher should do. Take `onrtac:<uuid>`: `substring(3,5)` is `"ta"`, which isn't equal to `"ac"`, so the matcher just falls through to the UUID check and passes. A token issued with the wrong grant would pass too. The assertions in `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` therefore only check that the value is `xxx:<uuid>`, not which grant issued it. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also check `items[0].length() == 6` first. Note that once this is fixed, any flow where the grant attribute isn't set (it falls back to `na`) will start failing these assertions.

rawTokenId null check actually checks grantType again

`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` passes `grantType` again, so a null `rawTokenId` is never rejected. If one gets through, `encodeTokenId` builds an id ending in `:null`. Change the argument to `rawTokenId`.

New abstract getShortcut() breaks custom grant factories, and the shortcut length isn't checked

`getShortcut()` is abstract with no default. Every third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` will now fail to compile or load, and a factory that returns null makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw an NPE in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` (lines 75-76), which aborts server startup. The decoder also requires exactly 2 characters per segment (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81`), but nothing checks the length of a custom shortcut. A 3-letter shortcut (which the Javadoc says is the usual form) produces token ids that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Options: validate the length (exactly 2) and non-null in `postInit` with a clear error, fix the Javadoc's "3-letters" wording, and possibly add a default implementation.
